lina (ML Eng): FYI onboarding smoke for cetus-40k-int3 hitting a deterministic divergence at prefill boundary ~8192 tokens. Not subtle, full failure on long QA traces. :grimacing:
otto (research): Do you mean outputs suddenly change or do we get decoding errors/NaNs?
lina (ML Eng): Outputs change — coherent until ~8191 then next tokens drift. No NaNs. FP16 baseline is fine. Repro included.
lina (ML Eng): repro gist:
```
# simplified repro
model = load('cetus-40k', quant='int3-compact')
primer = system_prompt + long_user_block(8200)
res_fp16 = run(model_fp16, primer)
res_int3 = run(model_int3, primer)
assert compare(res_fp16, res_int3) == fail at offset 8192
```
otto (research): 8192 smells like a power-of-two pack/workspace wrap. Do we have KV index traces?
lina (ML Eng): I dumped runtime KV pointers: on int3 run the write pointer resets to 0 at 8192 while read pointer continues at 8192 -> off-by-window. fp16 shows no wrap. snippet:
```
INT3 KV_WRITE_BASE: 8192 -> 0
INT3 KV_READ_IDX: 8192 -> 8192
```
kai (infra): Could be a ring-buffer modulo bug in the packed buffer codepath (pack unit = 4096 entries?). We recently changed the packing stride for int3 to optimize memcpy.
otto (research): Another angle: RoPE phase multipliers are computed from absolute token index; if indices are folded incorrectly after wrap you get phase shift and semantic drift.
Sam (platform): We need an immediate customer mitigation. Options: 1) route long-prefill (>8000) away from int3, 2) force a soft prefill split that restarts the pack so we never hit wrap, 3) degrade to int4 for those requests. Thoughts?
lina (ML Eng): soft prefill split may be least invasive — we can chunk requests at 8k boundaries and stitch outputs, but that might affect latency. Routing fallback to int4 is straightforward but ups costs.
kai (infra): I'll add a diagnostic flag in runtime: when pack_wrap_detected++ emit full KV dump to S3 for triage. Also will add an assertion in packed memcpy that fails in debug builds when write pointer < last_max.
otto (research): I'll prototype a tiny C harness that reproduces packed memcpy wrap on local machine. If it's the stride math we can patch quickly.
evalbot: Nightly long-context job scheduled for cetus-40k on staging: will run int3/int4/fp16 variants and post diffs in this thread tomorrow morning.
Sam (platform): I'll prepare a routing rule to send requests with prefill_len >= 8000 to int4 variant on staging (canary 10%). We'll hold prod until we confirm fix.
lina (ML Eng): Filed INFR-9421 with artifacts and raw KV dumps: https://redwood.internal/issues/INFR-9421. Owners: otto for C repro, kai for runtime asserts/logging, sam for routing. Thanks. :rocket:
